title: Mormons Go Nuclear
description: Deseret goes atomic with a fleet of desert reactors. Ask why. The faithful are prepared — the market only thinks it is.

companies.name: Beehive Atomics
companies.description: Factory-builds truckable sealed reactors; its planned west-desert fleet is water-cooled, and the faith's endowment wrote its founding check.

companies.name: Perpetual Reserve Trust
companies.description: The faith's investment arm: a famously quiet endowment holding founding stakes across the corridor's industry, and more cash than it has ever disclosed.

companies.name: Promised Valley Ranches
companies.description: Cuts alfalfa and runs cattle on the faith's old welfare ranches in the west desert, on water rights filed by the first settlers — the basin's most senior.

companies.name: Year's Supply Co.
companies.description: Sells freeze-dried pantries, water barrels, crank radios and iodine tablets by catalog and warehouse store to households keeping a year of reserves.

companies.name: Everbloom Botanicals
companies.description: Blends essential oils and herbal drops sold entirely through a downline of independent home distributors, each of whom recruits the next.

companies.name: Bonneville Concrete & Grade
companies.description: Pours ready-mix from its own gravel pits and has graded half the corridor's highways, dams and chapel lots — though never once built to a nuclear spec.

companies.name: Red Mesa Milling
companies.description: Runs the country's last licensed uranium mill on a remote desert mesa, buying ore from mothballed canyon mines and stockpiling yellowcake.

companies.name: Intermountain Light & Coal
companies.description: The incumbent utility: aging coal units and gas peakers selling firm power to the valley and, under long contract, to cities out of state.

companies.name: Alpine Rack & Compute
companies.description: Builds server halls along the tech corridor for out-of-state clouds; has land and permits banked, and waits years in the grid queue for every megawatt.

companies.name: Saltair Minerals
companies.description: Harvests magnesium and lithium from evaporation ponds on the shrinking salt lake; the basin's single largest buyer of electricity.

companies.name: Glory Dome Ministries
companies.description: Prosperity-gospel broadcaster beaming nightly from a chrome mega-dome to nine million believers; pledge drives are the whole income statement.

companies.name: Called & Ready Outfitters
companies.description: Fits departing nineteen-year-old missionaries with two years of suits, bicycles and luggage from storefronts beside every training center.
